brackets_single.note: Statutory brackets, not CPI-indexed; unchanged for several years.

senior_addl_exemption_mfj.unit: $ per qualifying spouse age 65+ on a joint return

social_security.note: Fully exempt from NJ gross income tax regardless of income.

line28a_worksheet_note.value: Per NJ-1040 2025 instructions, Line 28a: Line A = actual pension/annuity/IRA income; Line B = $100,000 flat (MFJ, income <= $100k), 50% of Line A (income $100,001-$125,000), or 25% of Line A (income $125,001-$150,000); exclusion = lesser of Line A or Line B. So in the 50%/25% tiers the reduction applies to the taxpayer's actual retirement income, not to the $100,000 cap.

retirement_income.note: Retirement/Pension Exclusion: filer (or spouse) must be 62+ or disabled as of Dec 31, AND total income must be <= $150,000. If income <= $100,000: exclude up to the cap ($100k MFJ/$75k single/$50k MFS). If $100,001-$125,000: 50% of the otherwise-allowed exclusion. If $125,001-$150,000: 25%. Above $150,000: $0 -- the entire exclusion is lost (hard cliff), not just the excess, and all pension/401(k)/IRA income is fully taxed as ordinary income.

senior_tax_credits.note: The $1,000 age-65+ personal exemption plus the Pension/Retirement Income Exclusion above are NJ's senior-specific income tax breaks.

effective_rate_pct.unit: % of home value/year, statewide avg effective rate
effective_rate_pct.note: Highest in the nation; Tax Foundation's CY2023-data figure is 2.23%.

property_tax.relief_programs_note: $250 Senior/Disabled Property Tax Deduction: age 65+/disabled, NJ resident 1+ year, income <= $10,000 (excludes Social Security) -- income limit far below typical retirement-planning income, unlikely to apply. Senior Freeze (Property Tax Reimbursement): age 65+ or SSDI, NJ resident 10+ years, in current home 3+ years, 2025 income limit $172,475 -- reimburses property tax increases above a locked base-year amount. Stay NJ (new, benefits from 2025/2026): age 65+ (or SSDI), income < $500,000 -- credit = 50% of property tax bill, capped at $6,500 (income <$100k)/$5,000 ($100k-$150k)/$4,000 ($150k-$200k) and phasing out further above that, coordinated with Senior Freeze/ANCHOR via a 'maximum benefit' rule. ANCHOR: broader (non-senior-exclusive) rebate up to $1,750. None of these are applied to the estimate below since eligibility depends on income not modeled here.
